content:
Hi all, I opened a draft PR adding Corrádi's intersection lemma for finite set families:

https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/39936

The current version lives in Mathlib/Combinatorics/SetFamily/Corradi.lean and builds locally. It now exposes two main statements:

  • Finset.corradi_mul_le, the underlying Nat inequality
    m^2 * a^2 + m * N * b ≤ m * N * a + m^2 * N * b;

  • Finset.corradi_card_le_real, the standard real-valued ratio form
    m * (a^2 - b * N) ≤ N * (a - b).

The proof uses the usual double-counting argument plus Cauchy-Schwarz on the cover-count function
x ↦ #{i | x ∈ As i}.

Before polishing further, I’d appreciate design feedback on two points:

  1. Is Mathlib/Combinatorics/SetFamily/Corradi.lean the right location?

  2. Should the proof introduce/use this local coverCount API, or would reviewers prefer it to be phrased using the existing double-counting API in
    Combinatorics/Enumerative/DoubleCounting.lean, especially bipartiteBelow / bipartiteAbove?

Also happy to adjust theorem names or the choice of headline statement if there is a preferred mathlib style here.

I think this is the right location for this lemma. coverCount is not part of your final statements, so I would suggest either making it private, or replacing it with the existing double-counting API.
Let me also point out to you the mathlib AI policy: https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/#use-of-ai. In addition, you mention that the authors take responsibility for the mathematical content, but the reference to Jukna is currently seemingly hallucinated, as the quoted Lemma 5.5 is to an entirely different statement.

Thanks, this is helpful.

I’ll make coverCount private unless I end up replacing it with the existing double-counting API.

On the reference: yes, thanks for catching that. I’ll remove or correct the Jukna citation before marking the PR ready for review. The PR is still draft, so I’m using it to sort out exactly these issues before polishing.

I took a closer look at the PR, and it looks to me like it will need heavy changes before it's ready for mathlib, and so is quite likely to be unreviewed and closed as AI slop, for reasons described here: https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/287929-mathlib4/topic/What.20to.20do.20with.20.22slop.22.20PRs/near/587705509 as well as described in the AI policy linked above, especially because the proofs appear like they were generated with an LLM with no human input.

Hi Bhavik & Yan,

I very much value your time. I'm a genuine human (Andrew :wave:) and the motivation behind this Zulip chat is to learn the Mathlib process of collaboration (Mathlib is a respected and useful tool).

I want to learn more about this both for the benefit of the community and to also improve my own process of collaboration ("this is how mathlib does it").

I have now read both the resources you've provided and since this is the Mathlib way of doing things I am happy to agree to not further use any AI tools with respect to this discussion nor the PR.

I genuinely use the mentioned theorem in a formalization of recent work in coding theory (https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/2051, https://github.com/z-tech/z-lean/tree/main/LinearCodes). I continue to build on top of this for research purposes.

When I thought about what pieces from this effort could conceivably be upstreamed to Mathlib my objective was to identify the smallest discrete unit plausible for contribution as a learning process. Being that this is only ~100 lines I am open to dedicate the time to write this entirely by hand (if that's what's being requested) as I see this as a good learning opportunity.

Since this code works for my purposes already, I'd need an example or other instruction for how to do about this. Maybe you could suggest to me a lemma / file already in Mathlib that is sort of like the gold standard to help me understand "write the contribution in this way?"

If this proposed addition (irrespective of format) is genuinely not helpful there are of course no hard feelings.

Cheers,
Andrew
